summary: Review a queue-led preservation task and three rotated fresh searches; add six source-backed projects, retain one curated index and close the Follin component-splitting task.
notes: The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved source/target CPU areas before selection. Six new records and the updated Follin record therefore use only explicit primary CPU evidence. No project was independently compiled or executed.

project.title: Sharp PC-1500 ROM Disassembly
project.display_title: Sharp PC-1500 / TRS-80 PC-2 ROM disassembly
project.status: Documented TASM rebuild; not independently built

identity.narrative: The README identifies one LH5801 assembly reconstruction covering the A01, A03 and A04 Sharp PC-1500 ROM revisions, also applicable to the Radio Shack TRS-80 PC-2 lineage.

classification.narrative: This is a ROM disassembly/reconstruction with revision-selectable source and generated binaries; it is not presented as recovered original Sharp source.

source_cpu.narrative: The primary assembly filename, source comments and TASM build switch explicitly identify the historical ROM instruction set as Sharp LH5801.

target_cpu.narrative: The documented build invokes TASM's 5801 table and emits PC-1500 ROM binaries, explicitly retaining LH5801 as the output architecture.

build.narrative: The README and batch script document TASM commands for A01, A03 and A04 outputs and the repository contains generated BIN/LST files.
build.limitations: The tracker did not execute TASM or compare the generated binaries with Original_ROMs; runtime and byte identity remain unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed README, assembly and build script establish ROM targets but do not state minimum machine, RAM or peripheral requirements beyond product identity.

ai.narrative: The inspected README, source and build script contain no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The repository treats Sharp PC-1500 and Radio Shack TRS-80 PC-2 as the same ROM-family subject and keeps the three published ROM revisions in one coherent source file.

project.title: CalvaDOS
project.display_title: CalvaDOS — Genie IIIs hard-disk OS reconstruction

runtime_profiles.name: Stage B reconstruction
runtime_profiles.notes: Documented boot path uses the reconstructed Stage B OMTI hard-disk system; it runs on a physical Genie IIIs via the patch disk or under sdltrs-MultiHDC. No RAM floor is stated.

project.status: Stage B boots and reads a real hard-disk directory according to the author

identity.narrative: The project explicitly reconstructs the lost Stage B CalvaDOS modification for the TCS Genie IIIs from surviving GDOS material, an OMTI boot EPROM, work disks and period documentation.

classification.narrative: The README repeatedly distinguishes this reconstruction from the unrecovered 1986 binaries and separates new BSD-licensed code from preserved third-party G-DOS-derived material.

source_cpu.narrative: The README identifies the Genie IIIs as a Z80 machine and documents Z80 disassembly/assembly as the reconstruction basis.

target_cpu.narrative: The reconstructed Stage B system and boot EPROM target the same Z80-based Genie IIIs hardware; no host CPU is substituted.

build.narrative: The author reports that the reconstruction boots from hard disk, reaches a command prompt, reads volume 5 and creates RAMDISK; source, disk images and build tools are present.
build.limitations: One known defect remains open, and the tracker did not independently assemble or boot the system.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README documents physical Genie IIIs and sdltrs-MultiHDC execution paths for the Stage B OMTI reconstruction, but states no minimum RAM.

ai.narrative: The reviewed README describes the manual tools and sources used but contains no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: CalvaDOS is reconstructed from stock G-DOS 2.4 plus surviving Club80-era hard-disk modifications; related emulator, stock-GDOS and disk-extraction repositories are explicitly named without being collapsed into this record.

project.title: PAKET
subjects: PAKET game definition language and compiler
project.status: Version 1.0 compiler with documented CPC 464 and MSX outputs

identity.narrative: The README identifies PAKET 1.0 as a game-definition language and compiler for point-and-click adventures targeting Amstrad CPC 464 and MSX.

classification.narrative: This is substantial original retro-development tooling, not a reverse-engineered game; one CPC tape library explicitly derives and simplifies required routines from firmware disassembly.

source_cpu.narrative: PAKET is a modern Java-authored compiler/game engine rather than reconstruction of one original machine-code subject, so an original source CPU is not applicable.

target_cpu.narrative: The emitted CPC/MSX templates explicitly use Zilog Z80 notation and the compiler includes a Z80 assembler-output utility, directly evidencing the output architecture.

build.narrative: The repository supplies a build script, Java compiler sources, examples and target templates; the README states that the compiler generates game binaries.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile the Java tool or execute a generated game.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed documentation names CPC 464 and MSX targets but gives no explicit minimum RAM, model revision or OS/ROM requirements suitable for a compatibility profile.

ai.narrative: The inspected README and target sources contain no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: PAKET incorporates credited WYZTracker player material and a CPC cassette layer derived from firmware disassembly, while the compiler and game-definition system remain the repository's coherent original project.

project.title: ROM Fiend
project.display_title: ROM Fiend — Macintosh ROM structure template for Hex Fiend
project.status: Parses common 68k and Old World PowerPC Macintosh ROM structures

identity.narrative: The README identifies a Hex Fiend file template for inspecting and modifying classic Macintosh Declaration and System ROMs.

classification.narrative: This is reusable ROM structure-analysis tooling with explicit parsing and error handling, not a ROM collection or emulator.

source_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly covers ROMs for 68k and Old World PowerPC Macs, and the template names PowerPC CPU resource variants.

target_cpu.narrative: ROM Fiend emits a structured Hex Fiend view rather than a port or reconstructed machine-code binary, so no output CPU applies.

build.narrative: Installation copies or symlinks the Tcl template and optional symbol maps into Hex Fiend; there is no compiled target build.
build.limitations: The tracker did not install the template or parse a ROM.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README requires Hex Fiend but gives no explicit host OS version, CPU or memory minimum; target Macintosh hardware requirements do not apply to the analysis template.

ai.narrative: The inspected README and template contain no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: ROM Fiend extends Hex Fiend through its template mechanism and optionally installs external Macintosh ROM symbol maps; those dependencies are not represented as reconstructed subjects here.

project.title: dF80
project.status: Documented M80/L80 rebuild is byte-identical to F80.COM

identity.narrative: The author identifies a partly commented reconstruction of Microsoft FORTRAN-80 3.4 for CP/M, including both 1985 F80 and 3.44 source variants.

classification.narrative: This is binary-derived compiler reconstruction; module boundaries were recovered by comparing multiple executables rather than from original Microsoft source.

source_cpu.narrative: The README states that the compiler produces Z80 assembler listings and that the recovered source is assembled with Microsoft's M80/L80 toolchain.

target_cpu.narrative: The reconstructed Z80 assembly emits CP/M F80.COM executables, explicitly preserving the Z80 output architecture.

build.narrative: The README gives M80 and L80 commands and claims the resulting F80.COM and F.COM executables are completely identical to their originals.
build.limitations: Byte identity is an author claim; the tracker did not run M80/L80 or compare binaries.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The project identifies CP/M executables but gives no minimum CP/M version, RAM, machine model or operating environment.

ai.narrative: The inspected README and recovered source contain no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The author distinguishes the selected CP/M compiler from a likely earlier TRS-80 lineage and from W. Cirsovius's separate M80/L80 disassemblies; neither is collapsed into this record.

project.title: Computer Archeology
project.display_title: Computer Archeology — annotated disassemblies and rendering toolchain
project.status: Large maintained corpus of annotated analyses with dedicated rendering and consistency tools

identity.narrative: The root repository contains the source analyses and Python toolchain behind computerarcheology.com, spanning many individually documented games and machines under one coherent publication system.

classification.narrative: This is both a maintained corpus of annotated binary disassemblies and reusable archaeology tooling; tracking the root preserves the shared renderer, memory-map conventions and analysis identity without splitting every title directory.

source_cpu.narrative: Reviewed content includes 6502, Z80, 6809 and 8080 program analyses; only those directly represented instruction sets are recorded, not every platform suggested by directory names.

target_cpu.narrative: The common project output is linked documentation, analysis data and web tooling rather than reconstructed machine-code binaries with one target CPU.

build.narrative: The README documents Python commands for generating and serving the site and describes automated name/link maintenance across disassembly and memory-map files.
build.limitations: The tracker did not execute the renderer or validate individual title binaries.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed root documentation does not provide host CPU, RAM or Python-version minima for the analysis/rendering toolchain.

ai.narrative: The inspected root documentation and tooling source contain no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The title directories share one rendering/annotation architecture and publication site, so the repository is represented as one broad analysis project rather than speculative directory-scoped records.

runtime_profiles.name: Modern AY example snapshots
runtime_profiles.platform: ZX Spectrum / Amstrad CPC AY workflow
runtime_profiles.notes: README documents sjasmplus builds of exec_ examples to .sna snapshots and execution in ZEsarUX. No minimum model or RAM is stated.

project.status: Recovered multi-title source archive; documented Z80 AY example rebuilds

identity.narrative: This remains one coherent preservation archive of Tim and Geoff Follin music data and drivers recovered from Tatung Einstein disks; individual game-named folders are archival components, not independently published projects.

classification.narrative: The archive combines original period 6502/Z80 source recovery, a reverse-engineered token detokenizer and modern example rebuild work; it is not a game disassembly collection.

source_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly identifies original C64 6502 and CPC/Spectrum Z80 source material recovered from the disks.

target_cpu.narrative: The documented modern build lane assembles selected Z80 AY examples with sjasmplus into snapshots; no rebuilt 6502 output is claimed.

build.narrative: The README documents VS Code build tasks for exec_ files, producing .sna snapshots for ZEsarUX; other recovered files remain source material without blanket rebuild claims.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build the examples, and no compile claim is generalized to every disk or title.

runtime_profiles.narrative: A bounded Z80 AY snapshot workflow is explicit; no minimum Spectrum/CPC model, RAM or ROM revision is given.

ai.narrative: The README and reviewed archive structure contain no development-AI disclosure; absence does not establish non-use.

relationships.narrative: The per-game and per-disk materials share the same donor provenance, recovery process, drivers and detokenization workflow; repository-root scope is the accurate catalogue identity.

Other returned emulator/framework matches did not establish a new candidate.
